title: An anti-aliasing RC filter
story: A vibration sensor's useful signal is below 100 Hz, and the ADC samples at 10 000 samples per second. Anything near or above the 5 kHz Nyquist frequency will fold back and pollute the readings. A 100 nF capacitor is fitted; choose the resistor of the RC low-pass in front of the ADC so the signal at 100 Hz loses less than 1 dB while anything at 5 kHz is attenuated by at least 12 dB.

goals.label: signal at 100 Hz loses less than 1 dB
at least 12 dB of attenuation at 5 kHz

hints: The cutoff frequency is f_c = 1 / (2 pi R C).
Well above the cutoff, a first-order RC loses about 20 dB for every factor of 10 in frequency.
The cutoff must sit well above 100 Hz but well below 5 kHz: try each resistor with C = 100 nF.
